title: Legacy VR controller migration and private-read gate
classification: Confirmed synthetic local cross-account cache disclosure; focused fix verified; full app/headset acceptance remains open

environment.fixture: Owned ephemeral loopback static server, synthetic adult/child data; external page requests blocked; no application/database/operator credentials

original_trigger.observation: Actual old /vr worker remained controller after settled root registration; cached synthetic adult VR response remained readable offline after logout and simulated account switch. Four mitigation regression cases initially failed.

verification.browser_scope: Owned /vr and /vr/ registrations, query-bearing scripts, root absent/already active, delayed old response, logout link/button, first load/no worker support, failed legacy update, rejected/hung optional root install, unrelated registration/cache preservation, versioned asset caching, private/API/cover exclusion, data-free offline shell and post-logout offline network failure
verification.review: Fresh isolated read-only investigator and one fresh candidate reviewer; reviewer found optional-install fallback regression, reproduced as two browser failures then corrected and passed. Child usage excluded from root model comparison.
verification.cleanup: Fresh browser contexts/browsers closed; owned loopback servers stopped and joined; no product/database/prod mutations
verification.pinned_fixture_line_endings: Explicit LF checkout rule preserves byte-pinned legacy scripts on Windows; git check-attr verifies both paths.

design: Shared installer updates owned legacy registrations and verifies safe replacement control before private VR catalog/detail requests; page stops recreating retired scope.
A data-free retirement controller can stay attached until navigation; policy acknowledgement establishes safe control, then a navigation selects the root worker.
Root claim acknowledgement supports an already-active root; logout directly deletes owned caches even without a controller and preserves unrelated caches.
Unknown/unsafe legacy control fails closed; optional root installation failure does not block browsing once control is verified safe.
rework: Initial unit harness omitted its shell provider; corrected before valid reproduction. Private fetch assertions were narrowed to VR requests rather than unrelated loading-icon requests.
Consolidated overlapping installer/API edits observed during continuation. Initial implementation accidentally nested readiness setup and failed browser execution; corrected.
An assumed root-controller transition was too strong for the actual unregistered retirement lifecycle; explicit policy acknowledgement plus subsequent navigation is verified.
Polling the old active worker with messages interfered with activation; probe once before updating, then acknowledge the replacement.
Post-logout clears the offline fallback too, so offline navigation may fail rather than render that page. Tests distinguish pre-logout data-free fallback from post-logout network failure.
limitations: Synthetic browser account fixtures do not establish authenticated Oneirodex/headset acceptance, deployed cookie/session/ACL behavior, or all supported browser versions.
A fully offline client with only old code cannot receive migration until online.
No full-route parity promotion, production deployment, release, default-branch alert resolution, or full unrestricted Python/coverage acceptance.
Member suite emitted existing React act warnings; build emitted existing bundle warnings.
